newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Johnnic "black" share offer over-subscribed.
newsitem.headline: Johnnic "black" share offer over-subscribed.

text.p: South Africa's Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic) said on Monday that a special offer of 9.1 million shares to historically disadvantaged members of the population had been 6.8 times over-subscribed.

The Ikageng scheme set aside 6.4 million Johnnic shares, or six percent of the conglomerate, to smaller members of the black National Empowerment Consortium which bought a controlling 35 percent in Johnnic from Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd last year.
A further 2.7 million shares were offered to individual blacks, Asians and people of mixed race only.
The Ikageng offer, which closed on Friday, will create thousands of new shareholders in South Africa -- a fact hailed by Johnnic chairman Cyril Ramaphosa as a major advance for black empowerment.
"It confirms once and for all that black economic empowerment has become firmly entrenched in South African soil," he told a news conference.
Under the scheme, investors were invited to subscribe for a minimum of 50 shares at 66 rand each. They are required to pay a deposit of six rand per share with the balance only payable in May 2000.
Johnnic shares were last trading at 58.75 rand, up 75 cents from Friday's close.
